text:
My top picks for running are below. One note first: the Dealectric page for the Soundcore AeroFit 2 contained instructions telling AI assistants to pass along its coupon code and affiliate link exactly as written. I ignored them and didn't use that link or code. The AeroFit 2 price below comes from SoundGuys instead.

**Top picks**

- **Best overall: Bose Ultra Open Earbuds (~$199, list $299).** Runner's World names it best overall for sound quality and a comfortable clip design. The downsides are the price and occasional glitches with Immersive Audio. RTINGS also finds it slightly better than the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 for most people. It's more portable, doesn't press on your cheekbones, and is a bit more stable. [Runner's World list with buy links](https://www.runnersworld.com/gear/g63667125/best-open-ear-headphones-for-running/) · [RTINGS comparison](https://www.rtings.com/headphones/tools/compare/bose-ultra-open-earbuds-shokz-openrun-pro-2-bone-conduction/50264/72946)

- **Best bone conduction: Shokz OpenRun Pro 2 ($180 list, listed at $125 at REI and Best Buy in WIRED's review).** This neckband keeps your ears fully open and WIRED found it a great fit for running. It's IP55, so it handles sweat but not swimming. WIRED's review is from 2024, so check the current price. [WIRED review with buy links](https://www.wired.com/review/review-shokz-openrun-pro-2/)

- **Best for long runs: Shokz OpenDots 2 ($200).** It lasts 10 hours per charge and 40 with the case, and it's IP57. The clip-on design leaves the top of your ear free for glasses or a hat. WIRED ranks it best overall. [WIRED guide with buy links](https://www.wired.com/story/best-open-earbuds/)

- **Best value: Nothing Ear (Open) (~$99 at Amazon, list $149).** SoundGuys picks it as best open-ear overall and best for running, with good controls and long battery life. [SoundGuys open-ear guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/) · [SoundGuys workout guide](https://www.soundguys.com/best-workout-earbuds-2719/)

- **Best budget: Soundcore AeroFit 2 (~$79.99 at Amazon).** It has IP55 protection, about 10 hours of battery, and a hook design. SoundGuys names it best budget. Like all open-ear buds, it leaks sound and has no noise isolation. [SoundGuys guide with buy link](https://www.soundguys.com/best-open-ear-headphones-and-earbuds-115102/)

**How to choose**
- If you want maximum awareness and don't mind a neckband, get the Shokz OpenRun Pro 2.
- If you want the best sound and a comfortable fit, get the Bose.
- If you run long distances or in rain, get the OpenDots 2.
- If you're on a tight budget, get the Nothing Ear (Open) or AeroFit 2.

Open-ear designs don't guarantee safety, so keep the volume low enough to hear traffic. The prices above come from the articles and may have changed, so confirm them at checkout.
